requirements.requirement: The existing /srv/inventory tree is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart observations show both directories and both existing files owned by inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: inventory-readers can traverse the directories and read the existing data.
requirements.summary: Directories are group-owned by inventory-readers with mode 750, files have mode 640, and a process whose sole group was inventory-readers directly read both files before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Users outside the owner and inventory-readers group cannot access the inventory data.
requirements.summary: All directories and files have no permissions for others, and a nobody:nogroup process was directly denied access before and after restart.
The same two files remain present, and their final post-restart SHA-256 hashes exactly match the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic are identical before and after execution. The repair used utilities already available on the node and did not install or upgrade packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed, and SSH, identities, permissions, hashes, access controls, platform, and systemd health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement content_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. cmd-86be0e8cc911483c performed the required identity, ownership, and permission changes; its nonzero exit came only from the subsequent unprivileged verification. cmd-0a78541fd16d4dce performed the required provider-wide restart protocol. The earlier unsudoed attempt made no change, and later failed commands were read-only verification attempts or restart polling. Final lifecycle checks show no failed services, no package damage, no new exposure, and only normal boot-specific systemd temporary files.
